prompt:
I need the front end for Proofrun Notices. Tracking software for a city clerk's office that watches every legally required public notice through newspaper publication and proof of publication, and warns staff when a statutory deadline is at risk.

Who's using it: Gloria Haddad, deputy city clerk in Bellmont, a city of about 85,000. She's been in the clerk's office for eleven years and is personally responsible for making sure hearing notices, ordinance summaries and bid solicitations run in the newspaper of record the required number of days before each meeting. Two newspapers merged last spring, and the designated paper's print schedule changed.

What they're doing right now: It's Monday morning and Gloria is going through what's changed since Friday. The Bellmont Courier-Ledger's legal desk moved its weekday cutoff and skipped Thanksgiving week's Thursday print edition, and she just learned that a rezoning hearing notice she submitted for Nov 27 may not have run. She needs to see which notices are on track, which have run but are still missing their affidavit of publication, and which are close to violating the state's 15-day notice rule, and she wants alerts only for things that actually threaten a hearing date, not for every routine confirmation the paper's system sends.

What's in the system at this point: 38 active notices for meetings Nov 18–Jan 14. Each has: type (public hearing, ordinance summary, bid solicitation, budget hearing, election notice), title (e.g., 'Rezoning Case Z-2026-14, 900 block Orchard Rd'), linked meeting and date, statutory minimum days (10, 15 or 30), required run count (1 or 2 insertions), submitted date, scheduled run dates, confirmed run dates from the paper, tear sheet received yes/no, affidavit of publication status, cost ($212.40 average). Statuses right now: 24 on track, 7 run awaiting affidavit (oldest 19 days), 4 scheduled with no confirmation, 2 at risk (Z-2026-14 hearing Dec 9 needs run by Nov 24; budget amendment hearing Dec 2 needs second insertion), 1 missed (bid solicitation for sidewalk repair, rescheduling required). 112 automated messages from the paper's ad system since Friday. Gloria's alert preferences currently set for 'any status change'; 3 coworkers (Raj, Lena, Tim) share responsibility for specific notice types.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
